chunks: No power shall you have over (all) My creatures except those who fall into error and follow you,
ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have power over according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Hijr is often cited to demonstrate that Satan's dominion is contingent upon human free will rather than divine compulsion, specifically highlighting the 'ghawin' (those astray) who actively align with him. This distinction underscores the theological principle that while all of God's servants are potentially protected, Satan gains authority only over those who consciously choose his path of deviation.
